messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: convergence in stan
parts:
Hi,

Did anybody experience "funny" convergence issues: after running 1000 warm-up and 1000 draws first time there is no convergence.  When the same sampling procedure is repeated the second time convergence is fine.  I don't set the seed and instead of stan function use a sequence of stanc, stan_model, and sampling functions (the code is below - I have made the chains to run in parallel in Windows).

I am using 2.3.0 version of stan.

Thanks for any suggestions,
Linas

stanmod <- function (chain, sm, data, warmup, n.draws, pars, init) {
    if (length (init) == 1) {
        if (init == "random") {
            init <- "random"
        } else {
            init <- list (init [[chain]])
        }
    } else {
        init <- list (init [[chain]])
    }
    sampling (sm, data = data, pars = pars, chains = 1,
        iter = warmup + n.draws, warmup = warmup,
        init = init, 
        diagnostic_file = paste (chain, "d.txt", sep = ""),
        sample_file = paste (chain, "s.txt", sep = ""),
        verbose = TRUE, refresh = max ((warmup + n.draws) / 10, 1),
        chain_id = chain)
}
par.stan <- function (file, code, data, warmup, n.draws, chains, pars,
    init)
{
    # translate model to C++
    rt <- stanc (file, model_code = code, model_name = file)
    if (rt$status == FALSE) return (NULL)
    # compile C++ code
    sm <- stan_model (stanc_ret = rt, verbose = FALSE)
    cat ("COMPILED\n")
    cl <- makePSOCKcluster (chains, outfile = "outfile.txt")
    setDefaultCluster (cl)
    clusterExport (NULL, c ('stanmod'))
    clusterEvalQ (NULL, library (rstan))
    posterior <- parLapply (NULL, 1 : chains, stanmod, sm, data, warmup,
        n.draws, pars, init)
    stopCluster (cl)
    return (posterior)
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: convergence in stan
parts:
On Tuesday, July 22, 2014 10:05:08 AM UTC-4, Linas Mockus wrote:
Did anybody experience "funny" convergence issues: after running 1000 warm-up and 1000 draws first time there is no convergence.  When the same sampling procedure is repeated the second time convergence is fine.  I don't set the seed and instead of stan function use a sequence of stanc, stan_model, and sampling functions (the code is below - I have made the chains to run in parallel in Windows).

That behavior can't be ruled out. With different seeds there are different starting values and in addition, the adaptation may result in different stepsizes depending on where in the parameter space the sampler tended to be. But it is also possible that the model might not be great for the data so you should look at the whole range of diagnostics.

Ben
